desc: Implement a brute-force BFS oracle on ordered pairs (a,b), a!=b, for small N to obtain exact answers.
Implement a random connected graph generator and a tester that compares brute-force answers against candidate structural formulas.
Implement the small-N Chinese-postman candidate support formula for validation.
Run the existing oracle/tester in enumerate/random/summary modes with candidate comparison enabled and classify mismatches (candidate underestimates oracle; no overestimates observed).

Formalize the schedulability condition that distinguishes valid two-token passing gadgets from arbitrary Chinese-postman supports (cycle with two distinct attachments, branch/three-arm cases, terminal-hub extra excursions).
Derive a scalable formula for the minimum swap length using distances, bridge/block-cut structure, shortest cycles, and shortest private excursions/arms.
Implement an efficient final solver for N,M up to 2e5 based on the derived formula, replacing brute_force in solve_from_data.
Validate the final solver against the oracle on all small enumerated graphs and many random small graphs, and ensure public samples pass.
